mainEntity.name: How are water, sewer, and electric utilities hooked up to a backyard cottage?

acceptedAnswer.text: A detached backyard cottage requires full utility connections, including plumbing for a bathroom and kitchen, electrical service, and dedicated heating and cooling. Practical options involve extending lines from the main home or arranging a secondary utility meter, depending on capacity and municipal rules. If the existing main electrical panel is nearly at capacity, it may require a subpanel or a service panel upgrade to support electric appliances and air conditioning. Plumbing requires sufficient pipe slope to tie into existing sewer or septic lines. Assessing utility capacity early prevents unexpected site excavation delays during construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: Utilities are either extended underground from the primary residence or connected via secondary service, depending on local codes, panel capacity, and site layout.
